newsitem.title: USA: St. Jude sees 1997 EPS below 1996 level.
newsitem.headline: St. Jude sees 1997 EPS below 1996 level.

text.p: St. Jude Medical Inc chief financial officer Stephen Wilson said Thursday the company expects lower earnings per share this year, compared with 1996, but significant improvement in 1998.

"It would be consistent that (earnings per share) numbers this year will be lower than last, with our issuing a lot of shares to affect the Ventritex transaction. But we don't expect that situation to last very long. Next year will be significantly better," Wilson told Reuters in an interview following St. Jude's annual shareholders meeting here.
The First Call consensus calls for 1997 earnings of $1.60 per share against $1.82 per share in 1996. The 1998 consensus forecast is for $2.29 per share.

St. Jude revenues this year will likely top $1.1 billion, chief executive Ronald Matricaria told shareholders. He added that revenues from the cardiac rhythm management division, which sells pacemakers and other products, this year will exceed $900 million.
"At the end of this year, we'll probably be in excess of $1.1 billion in net revenues. In CRM this year, we'll have over $900 million in sales," Matricaria said.
Total St. Jude revenues in 1996 were $808.8 million. Of that, cardiac rhythym management accounted for $504 million.

Matricaria said his sales forecast for 1997 includes about $200 million in revenues from Ventritex Inc, a California based maker of implantable defibrillators that St. Jude is acquiring in a $365-million stock deal.
Also included in the forecast was $100 to $150 million in estimated revenue from Telectronics Pacing Systems, which St. Jude acquired in November from Australia's Pacific Dunlop Ltd for $135 million.

"We had $500 million in CRM business last year. We're about to buy Ventritex with a run rate of $100 million, which we hope to double this year. With Telectronics, we think we can get its sales to $100 million to $150 million this year," Matricaria told Reuters.
Matricaria said St. Jude expects Telectronics will likely contribute to earnings by the end of the second quarter.
